## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Xíng yuàn pǐn shū* in 10 fascicles is [澄觀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%BE%84%E8%A7%80) Chéngguān's commentary on the *Pǔxián xíngyuàn pǐn* 普賢行願品 of [般若](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%88%AC%E8%8B%A5) Prajñā's *[40-fascicle Avataṃsaka](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0041)* (T0293, fascicle 40) — the chapter containing the famous *Pǔxián shí dà yuàn* 普賢十大願 ("Ten Great Vows of Samantabhadra") that became the canonical East Asian devotional liturgy. Chéngguān, who had served as polishing-prose master on Prajñā's translation team, was the natural commentator for the work; his commentary became the standard Tang reading.

**Abstract**

The work is conventionally datable to the period 798 – 838 CE, the bracket from the completion of [般若](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%88%AC%E8%8B%A5) Prajñā's translation of [T0293](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0041) (in which Chéngguān participated) to Chéngguān's death. The bracket adopted here reflects this window. The doctrinal substance — the *Pǔxián xíngyuàn pǐn*'s "Ten Great Vows" and the cosmological framework that supports them — is the foundational text of East Asian Pure Land and Huáyán devotional practice; Chéngguān's commentary is the authoritative Tang reading and was the basis for all subsequent East Asian commentary on the Ten Vows.

The work is preserved in the Manji *Xù zàng jīng* (X227) collection.
